title: Episode-aware stream batcher and KV residency smoothing
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We observe elevated tail latency (p95-p99) and suboptimal token throughput for mixed prompt/response workloads where short prompts trigger long responses and vice versa. The existing continuous batcher aggregates requests by arrival time and length buckets; however, this leads to frequent KV cache churn and GPU memory fragmentation when episodes (multi-turn dialog sequences) re-enter the system shortly after completion.

Proposal: Implement an "episode-aware" stream batcher that: (1) identifies request episodes/turns by session tokens or ephemeral request metadata; (2) assigns a lightweight episode affinity score to active slots so that subsequent turns for the same dialog preferentially reuse the same GPU slot (when capacity allows); and (3) applies KV residency smoothing which biases eviction thresholds to keep recently-used KV entries pinned a bit longer for active episodes. Combined with a background slab compaction pass that coalesces fragmented GPU allocations during low-util windows, this aims to reduce cold KV fills and reclaim memory in a controlled way.

Goals: reduce p99 latency by at least 15% for mixed-length workloads, increase KV hit rate by 8-12%, and reduce observed GPU fragmentation spikes that cause OOM during microbursts. Preserve end-to-end latency SLOs for non-episode traffic and avoid unfairly starving long-running batch slots.

High-level approach and components:
- Episode affinity window: a tunable time window (default 12s) after which affinity decays; affinity is implemented as a small bitmap/score attached to active slots to avoid heavy per-episode state.
- KV residency smoothing: introduce a per-KV-key decay multiplier to the eviction policy so keys used by high-affinity episodes have their eviction priority reduced for a short duration.
- Slot priority escalation: when episodes re-enter within the affinity window and the slot is still present, escalate that slot's priority to get first chance at placement in the next coalesced batch.
- Compact-and-drain pass: a low-priority background routine that triggers slab compaction + KV rebalancing when GPU utilization < 35% for a rolling 30s period.
- Fallbacks: if affinity causes excessive head-of-line blocking, degrade to length-first scheduling for 30s; affinity is constrained by a maximum fraction of slots (default 25%).

Why different from existing work: Prior tickets focused heavily on length-aware continuous batching and coarse KV thresholds. This ticket centers on episode continuity (dialog-level locality) and a smoothing eviction policy to reduce transient cold-starts for returning episodes — a different tradeoff between localized memory residency and global fairness.

Telemetry and metrics to gather:
- p50/p95/p99 latency (token and request), by episode vs stateless traffic
- KV cache hit rate and cold-fill rate (per model + per slot)
- GPU free slab fragmentation metric (percent fragmented vs compactable)
- Slot residency churn (how often slots are reused vs reallocated)
- Throughput (tokens/sec) and cost-per-token deltas
- Incidence of OOM or allocation stalls during microbursts

Acceptance criteria:
- p99 latency improved by >= 15% for our mixed prompt/response bench cluster (compare to baseline 2026-03-01 run)
- KV hit rate increases by >= 8% on the same benchmark
- No more than a 5% regression in latency for non-episode traffic
- Background compaction should not increase p95 by more than 3% during its run
- Feature has an opt-out flag per customer and can be limited to specific model families for rollout

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: affinity could cause slot hoarding, reducing throughput for new sessions. Mitigation: cap affinity slots to 25% and use decay timers; add telemetry to detect unfairness and auto-disable if throughput drops 5% below baseline.
- Risk: longer KV residency increases memory pressure. Mitigation: pair smoothing with compaction and adaptive eviction thresholds tied to global free memory.
- Risk: complexity adds CPU overhead. Mitigation: keep affinity computation amortized and use compact representations (8-bit scores).

Experiment plan:
1) Simulation run in local emulation (1d): replay 72h production traces with episode-affinity toggle and measure metrics.
2) Canary on single cluster (2 GPU machines) for 24–48h with low traffic model families and detailed telemetry.
3) Progressive ramp to 10% of traffic across clusters with dynamic kill-switch if any p99 regression > 10%.
4) Full rollout with per-customer opt-in over 2 weeks.

Implementation notes and tasks:
- runtime change: batcher to maintain ephemeral episode index and slot affinity (ENG runtime core)
- KV eviction change: add decay multiplier and per-key recent-actor tag (APIs in kv-manager)
- compaction: implement GPU slab compaction trigger in allocator and ensure safe preemption of low-priority slots
- testing: microbench harness for mixed-length dialogs, unit tests for affinity decay logic

Estimated rollout effort: 3 sprints (experimentation + runtime changes + canary + rollouts).
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency reduced >= 15% on mixed prompt/response benchmark
KV hit rate increased >= 8% versus baseline
Background compaction does not increase p95 by > 3%
Per-customer opt-out exists and is tested
experiments: Simulate with 72h production trace replay (local) — compare baseline and episode-affinity runs
Canary: single cluster, 24–48h, verbose telemetry (kv-hit, slot-churn)
Ramp: 10% traffic across clusters with dynamic rollback rule
A/B: compare cost-per-token and p99 for two config sets (affinity=12s vs affinity=6s)
decisions: Affinity window default=12s chosen after offline tuning (tradeoff between reuse and hoarding)
Affinity fraction cap default=25% to preserve fairness
Eviction smoothing implemented as multiplicative decay on priority (simpler than per-key TTL)
